scope: JVM CPU/GC/heap/RSS cover observed JVM lifetime, not isolated SQL/planning/encoding.
Task GC overlaps JVM GC; never add them. Sampled peaks may miss real peaks.
Proc IO includes waited-for children; do not sum raw Driver/Executor lifetime IO.
Common-live IO is sampled coexistence, not exact SQL/connector-only IO; other short-lived children remain possible.
rchar/wchar are not disk/network-only. Zero storage read bytes may reflect page cache.
Spark spill excludes connector metadata sort/replay; Result Size is not raw commit-message bytes.
limitations: Single host with two Executor JVMs, not a multi-worker-node network benchmark.
Same physical data inodes and warm OS caches; fresh query JVMs and reversed order do not ensure identical caches.
Two observations per mode/query: descriptive midpoint/range only, no p95, significance or throughput extrapolation.
Timers include planning, execution and the common validation consumer; exact isolated encoding/planning CPU is unavailable.
Independent exact checks are reused once per actual reader mode, outside query timing.
Controlled read-planning failure does not classify or prove repair of the production three-million-file exit137.
